chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the nail when it is ripped out and does not grow back, and comes out black and spoiled, [the blood money is] ten dinars. So if it comes out white, [the blood money is] five dinars.
He returned to the first chain and said: And he ruled regarding the exposure of the toes [or fingers], [it is] one-third of the blood money of the finger.
So if a man is struck and both his testicles are turned inside out, his blood money is four hundred dinars.

So if he is straddled [or crippled in walking] and cannot walk except with a slight walk that is not beneficial to him, his blood money is four-fifths of the blood money of the soul, being eight hundred dinars.
So if the back becomes hunched from it, then at that point his blood money is complete, being one thousand dinars.
And the swearing oaths regarding everything from that are six people, according to whatever his blood money reaches.
And the blood money of the rupture, if it is above the pubic area, is one-tenth of the blood money of the soul, being one hundred dinars.
So if it is in the pubic area and it pierces the membrane, so there occurs a swelling in one of the testicles, its blood money is two hundred dinars, being one-fifth of the [complete] blood money.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةُ: Swearing oaths (used to establish the right to blood money)
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money / compensation for injury or death
key_terms.دِيَةُ النَّفْسِ: The full blood money of the soul (typically 1000 dinars)
key_terms.فَحِجَ: To be crippled or have one's walking impaired (specifically from straddling)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for injury to the testicles or pubic area according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elaborates on the judicial rulings of Imam Ali (AS) regarding specific injuries to the nails, fingers, and male genitalia, establishing precise blood money (diyah) amounts based on the severity and functional impact of the wound. It highlights the jurisprudential principle that compensation is calibrated not just by physical loss but by the resulting impairment, such as the inability to walk or the rupture of the scrotum, while also specifying the number of oaths required for full payment. This text serves as a foundational source for Shia fiqh on 'udm' (specific injuries) and demonstrates the practical application of Quranic inheritance and compensation laws in early Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the nails, when it is ripped out and does not grow back, and blackness emerges and it rots, is ten Dinars.
So if whiteness emerges, so it is five Dinars’.
Referring to the first chain, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he (Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>) judged regarding exposure of the toes being one-third of the wergild of the toes.
So if a man is hit and both his testicles turn around, so its wergild is four hundred Dinars.
So if he has to straddle and is not able to walk except for a simple walk, which is not beneficial to him, so its wergild is four-fifths of the wergild of the soul, being a hundred Dinars.

So if he becomes hunch backed from it, so this is where is the complete wergild, being a thousand Dinars; and the sworn endorsements regarding everything from that is six people upon whatever his wergild reaches; and wergild of the rupture above the pubic area is a tenth of the wergild of the soul, being one hundred Dinars.

So if it was in the pubic area, so it violates the abdominal membrane, so there occurs a swelling in one of the testicles, so its wergild is two hundred Dinars, being a fifth of the (complete) wergild’.
